memory_lessons.applicability: The selected single-accumulator parent is slower than the measured four-vector-search variant; use the latter's search structure as a comparison point, not as proof of why it was faster.
memory_lessons.claim: The four-vector equality-search program was correct on all five supplied cases and measured 4.3046e-7 seconds over three repetitions. This is a measured candidate result, not a demonstrated causal effect of unrolling.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare it with a candidate that changes only the first-pass accumulator structure, then validate correctness before evaluating timings.

memory_lessons.applicability: The current experiment combines a changed first pass with the four-vector search; existing eight-vector results suggest search unroll factor should not be assumed to improve performance monotonically.
memory_lessons.claim: The four-accumulator/eight-vector-search program measured 4.5678e-7 seconds; the single-accumulator/eight-vector-search program measured 4.9326e-7 seconds. Both were valid, but these comparisons do not establish the cause of their differences.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: After this candidate, retain correctness-valid candidates and compare repeated timings by input pattern where available.

proposal.hypothesis: The catalog's single-accumulator first pass with a four-vector equality search measured 4.3046e-7 seconds, while four-accumulator variants paired with one- or eight-vector searches measured 5.2660e-7 and 4.5678e-7 seconds. Those results do not isolate the interaction. This candidate pairs four independent minimum accumulators with the four-vector search to test whether reducing first-pass dependency chains helps without losing the search loop's observed benefit. It preserves signed comparisons, earliest-match order, and tail handling; random and decreasing inputs may still differ in second-pass work.

retained: Change the first-pass minimum reduction to four independent AVX-512F accumulators over groups of four vectors, then combine accumulators and process remaining vectors and scalar tail.
Unroll the second-pass equality search across four vectors; examine vector masks in index order and use the lowest set lane to preserve earliest-index ties.
Retain bounds-safe vector remainder and scalar-tail paths, including nonpositive sizes and INT32 extrema.
